title: Do open permit records predict how long a permit and the build behind it take, better than each city's own averages?
lede: research programme: open permit feeds from Chicago, San Francisco and Austin loaded onto one schema; median permit issue lag is 0 days in all three, so duration targets are zero-inflated; no model run yet
summary: An open research programme on duration forecasting from public building-permit feeds. Session 1 wrote the proposal (12 checked works, four falsifiable hypotheses, time-split evaluation with conformal intervals) and probed the feeds: Chicago has 851,778 rows, all issued, so it cannot show permits never issued; San Francisco has 1,297,657 rows with 750,188 completed; Austin has 2,382,939 rows with 2,184,191 completed. NYC DOB NOW is excluded until its licence is checked. Session 2 built the loader, schema, datasheets and a manifest (row counts match the probe) and found the median application-to-issue lag is 0 days in all three cities (p90 56, 81, 142), with SF and Austin build times at a median of about 105 days. Descriptive only: no model has been run.
